artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission ruled on a matter involving Metropolitan New York Presbytery's handling of a session that permitted a woman to expound Scripture during worship and held services without sermons. The SJC remitted the matter to the Presbytery to complete its work and report to the Committee on Review of Presbytery Records, while critiquing the procedural manner in which the matter was referred to the SJC.

artifacts.title: BCO 40-5 Matter re NW Georgia
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC, pursuant to citation by the 50th General Assembly under BCO 40-5, found that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred egregiously in approving calls and installing three candidates as associate pastors through a constitutionally deficient election process (slate voting, standing vote, failure to record number of voters present). The SJC stayed all further proceedings and declined to annul the installations, finding no PCA precedent for such relief.

artifacts.synopsis: Tennessee Valley Presbytery approved without exception Session minutes planning a youth group Super Bowl Party on Sunday; the SJC denied the complaint because the record was insufficient to find Presbytery erred in its constitutional interpretation. A dissent by RE Eggert argued the complaint was judicially out of order because the SJC lacks constitutional authority to review a presbytery's session-records review decisions under BCO 40-2 and 40-3.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC ruled that Anna Lewis's BCO 40-5 report filed directly with the SJC was out of order, holding that the SJC's only responsibility under Chapter 40 arises upon referral from the General Assembly per RAO 16-10.c. Six members dissented, arguing the SJC has historically exercised direct jurisdiction over BCO 40-5 reports and that the majority's interpretation was overly narrow and a departure from settled precedent.

artifacts.title: Brown v. Northern California Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of TE Jones et al. against Louisiana Presbytery, finding that LAP erred in two ways: first, in failing to apply the correct constitutional standard for determining whether TE Wilkins had differences with the Westminster Standards (differences need not involve overt contradiction or denial, but can arise from different interpretations of wording or biblical exegesis); and second, in failing to adequately investigate and evaluate such differences as required by RAO 16-3(e)(5), thereby neglecting its duty to condemn erroneous opinions that injure the peace or purity of the church.

artifacts.synopsis: Central Carolina Presbytery sent a memorial alleging that TE J. Steven Wilkins of Louisiana Presbytery was teaching doctrines (Federal Vision/Auburn Avenue theology) in flagrant contradiction to the Westminster Standards regarding election, covenant, and baptism. The SJC, after extended proceedings and directing Louisiana Presbytery to re-examine TE Wilkins, found Louisiana Presbytery had not adequately addressed the concerns and directed it via amends to appear under BCO 40-5 to account for its actions.
